tier: Plus, 1 year (Basic and Pro priced alongside)

free_tier.stated: No free plan. Yearly prices read from the pricing page's plan data: Basic '$40.68 billed every year', Plus '$41.83 billed every year', Pro '$74.27 billed every year'. Monthly: Basic $12.99, Plus $14.99, Pro $19.99. 2-year: Basic '$59.77', Plus '$54.94', Pro '$93.37'. Cheapest yearly price is Basic at USD 40.68; the cheapest yearly plan that lists residential IPs is Plus at USD 41.83.
free_tier.notes: The 30-day money-back line is on every plan card. The visible default term on the page is 2 years; the yearly and monthly prices are in the page's embedded plan data, whose checkout links name plan_yearly_basic, plan_yearly_plus and plan_yearly_pro. The Basic card lists a 'Residential IPs' bullet while the comparison table shows '-' for Basic in the Residential IPs row and the plan blurb says 'data center IPs'; Plus is therefore the first plan that lists residential IPs unambiguously.

retention.stated: not applicable: a tunnel, not stored bytes

egress.terms: Unlimited data: 'Mysterium VPN is a subscription service with fixed monthly or yearly plans and unlimited data. You don't pay per GB.' The help center adds that the service has no service limitations, no data caps and no speed reductions, with fair-usage guidelines.

interface_detail: A tunnel through apps (Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, browser extensions, routers). Protocols: WireGuard and OpenVPN (OpenVPN not on Android). UDP: WireGuard runs over UDP; the OpenVPN option uses TCP. Port forwarding: unverified: no page read states it; the vendor's port article says the app selects ports automatically. SOCKS5: unverified: no page read states a SOCKS5 endpoint for the consumer VPN. Obfuscation: unverified: no obfuscation is stated; OpenVPN over TCP is offered for restricted networks. BitTorrent: unverified: no first-party page read states a rule.
tooling: The vendor's apps; a login with an emailed magic link. No public API for the consumer VPN is documented in the pages read.
chaining: A tunnel whose exits are labelled residential (Plus and Pro) or data center (Basic) by the vendor; the upstream sees a node operator's address, so reachability and speed depend on the individual node.

limits.value: none published: 'unlimited data. You don't pay per GB.'

exits are home connections of independent node operators ('Our 7,500+ residential IPs come from independent node operators who explicitly agreed to take part'), so speed and availability depend on the node chosen

limits_note: Concurrent devices are capped by plan: 6 on Basic, 10 on Plus, 15 on Pro (help center); the vocabulary has no kind for it.
binding_note: No byte quota or request rate is published; the decisive uncertainty is the class of the exit addresses, which is a vendor claim for the plans and is not a limit kind.

identity_cost.detail: An email address is the login and there is no password: 'MysteriumVPN does not use passwords for logging in, instead it requires an email address and access to the respective inboxes'; the magic link expires in 30 minutes. Payment: major cards, cryptocurrencies, in-app purchases, PayPal, Apple Pay and Google Pay.

reliability_note: Exits are home connections run by independent node operators, so a given node can go offline or slow; the vendor's help center says its OpenVPN option over TCP is the fallback where WireGuard (UDP) is blocked.
confidence_note: Documented for price, protocols, UDP and sign-up. The residential claim is a vendor claim ('7,500+ residential IPs from real people in 100+ countries'; 'Residential IPs are registered to real ISPs and real households'). The vendor's public discovery API labels every node with an ip_type, an ISP and an ASN, which makes the label inspectable: read for Latvia on 2026-11-04, the residential-filtered list names ISPs such as JSC Balticom (AS24651) and SIA Lattelekom (AS12578) and the hosting-filtered list names CGI Global Limited (AS56971). The API publishes no node IP, so no page lets a reader check a label against a registry, and which node a given Plus connection exits through is not published. Class of evidence for the residential claim: a vendor claim with a vendor-published label, documented but not measured against a registry. Measured would need connecting through the service and checking the exit address's registry and usage class.
price_per_tb_month: USD 41.83 billed yearly for Plus (USD 40.68 for Basic); a subscription price, not a per-TB price
